result.title: RELAY: Selective Self-Distillation with Adaptive Hand-off for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Rubric-based reinforcement learning grades a response against many written criteria but collapses them into one reward, which discards the detail the rubric carries and gives no GRPO reward gradient when a group's responses tie. A frozen teacher that reads the rubric as privileged context provides token-level supervision, but we observe an early plateau in the gains over GRPO. RELAY uses advantages and rewards to select positive-advantage and low-scoring zero-advantage rollouts, and monitors the distillation loss to decide when to retire the teacher. Stage 1 combines selective distillation from a frozen teacher with GRPO; a plateau detector then removes the teacher, and Stage 2 continues with GRPO alone. Calibrated on one model-domain pair and reused unchanged in three others, the plateau detector fires between steps 122 and 171. RELAY scores highest in-domain among the compared methods in all four settings, ahead of GRPO on RaR-Medicine by 4.62 points with Qwen3-1.7B and 6.02 with Qwen3-4B. On Qwen3-1.7B/Medicine, removing the teacher from a shared checkpoint outperforms keeping, weakening or refreshing it. Distilling selected rollouts covering about half the response tokens also outperforms distilling all rollouts at a matched average coefficient.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RELAY：在 rubric-based RL 中先用冻结教师对「正 advantage 与低分零 advantage」的 rollout 做选择性自蒸馏并叠加 GRPO，再通过平台期检测器在训练中撤除教师，转入纯 GRPO 阶段，并在多个模型—领域组合上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按 advantage 选择性蒸馏 + 依据损失平台期动态停止外部监督」的监督调度，可能为 latent 推理训练的贡献分配与监督何时撤除提供可核查线索，但该工作本身是纯文本 RL 训练，与视觉状态生成无直接联系。
